ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that the line segment \(AC=12\,\text{cm}\), and point \(B\) is on line segment \(AC\), satisfying \(BC=\frac{1}{2}AB\). What is the length of \(AB\)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal line segment, A is at the left end, C is at the right end, and B is marked on line segment AC and is located between A and C; D and E can also be seen in the figure on the same straight line, but this problem only needs the positional relationship of A, B, and C. Then reason: It is known that AC=12 cm, and BC=\frac{1}{2}AB. Let AB=x cm, then BC=\frac{x}{2} cm. Because B is between AC, AC=AB+BC, that is x+\frac{x}{2}=12. Solving gives \frac{3x}{2}=12, so x=8. Therefore AB=8 cm.
